title: Licensing Act 1857
definition: An emergency legislative measure enacted by Lord Canning during the Revolt of 1857 to impose strict state control over the press by mandating a government license for the publication and circulation of all printed materials.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the first major legislative attempt by the British to curb the 'freedom of the press' in response to political instability, serving as a precursor to the more draconian Vernacular Press Act of 1878.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Licensing Act 1857.
